title: The Claude-side Edit guards stop a Copilot patch-string edit of a committed binder
summary: Copilot CLI can hand a PreToolUse hook the raw apply_patch text as a string tool_input under tool_name Edit or Write. The Codex-twin guards in .codex-plugin/hooks/scripts/ already parse that string and deny a patch that touches a committed binder or a pack (G3, verified on zbook); the Claude-side guards in hooks/scripts/ still treat any non-dict tool_input as allow, so the same edit slips through wherever a consumer repo's .claude/settings.json routes Copilot to them. Port the patch handling to the two Claude-side scripts, with self-tests, and correct FINDINGS.md so G3 is marked done for both sides and the live Windows run of the Claude-side path is owed to G4.
motivation: FINDINGS.md G3 requires the patch-string normalizer in both hooks/scripts/ and .codex-plugin/hooks/scripts/, but only the Codex twins got it; the G3 row reads Done while half its spec is unmet.

included: hooks/scripts/guard_binder_immutability.py: parse a string tool_input that starts with *** Begin Patch, deny when a patch op touches a committed binder, allow an untracked draft, accept \ in patch paths
hooks/scripts/guard_pack_write.py: the same for pack files
--self-test cases in each script for the four G3 acceptance checks
FINDINGS.md G3 section and gap table: both sides done; Claude-side live Windows run recorded as a G4 acceptance check
excluded: any change to the Codex twins or the plugins/karta projection (already done and verified)
a shared normalizer module imported by all four guards (each guard stays single-file stdlib so any hook launcher on Windows can run it)
G4 itself: a consumer repo .github/hooks manifest or .claude/settings.json adaptation
live Copilot run of the Claude-side scripts on zbook (needs the G4 consumer-repo route; deferred there)

work_items.title: guard_binder_immutability.py (Claude side) denies a patch-string edit of a committed binder
work_items.summary: Port the Codex twin's patch handling into hooks/scripts/guard_binder_immutability.py so a string tool_input carrying an apply_patch body is parsed and judged like a dict edit.
work_items.contract: EDIT hooks/scripts/guard_binder_immutability.py only. Keep it a single stdlib-only file; no new imports from other repo modules. (1) NORMALIZE: when payload['tool_input'] is a str whose lstrip() starts with '*** Begin Patch', treat it as {'command': <string>} regardless of tool_name (Copilot sends Edit or Write; Codex sends apply_patch). A str tool_input that is not a patch still passes, as today. (2) PARSE: copy parse_patch_ops and DIRECTIVE_RE from .codex-plugin/hooks/scripts/guard_binder_immutability.py verbatim in behavior: directives '*** Add File:', '*** Update File:', '*** Delete File:', '*** Move to:'; every patch path has '\\' replaced by '/'; content lines are +/- prefixed so a directive-looking line inside file content cannot spoof an op. (3) JUDGE: for each op, resolve the path against payload cwd and apply the script's existing committed-binder rule: a path under .karta/binders/ (not archive/) that is a blob in HEAD of its repo is denied; a path that is not tracked in HEAD (an untracked draft) is allowed; paths outside the binder directory are ignored. Reuse the existing helpers for 'is this a committed binder' rather than adding a second notion; add a _tracked_in_head(path, cwd) helper modeled on the Codex twin only if the existing helpers need an absolute path first. A denied patch exits 2 with the script's existing deny message on stderr naming the binder path; an allowed one exits 0 with no stdout. (4) FAIL-OPEN posture unchanged: unreadable payload, non-git cwd, or any internal error exits 0. (5) SELF-TEST: extend --self-test with at least these cases, each exercised through the real main() against a temp git repo fixture: a bare '*** Add File: .karta/binders/x.json' string on a committed x.json is denied (exit 2); an '*** Update File:' string on a committed binder is denied; the same Update string on an untracked draft binder is allowed; a patch path spelled '.karta\\binders\\x.json' on a committed x.json is denied (the \\ path matches); a non-patch string tool_input still passes. Replace the current 'tool_input not a dict passes' case so it asserts the non-patch string specifically. The summary line stays in the exact form 'N/N checks passed' with N at least 27 (today 22). (6) No change to hooks/hooks.json: the Claude hook manifest already routes Edit|Write|MultiEdit to this script.

assertions: the script's own --self-test exits zero and its N/N summary parses with N at least 27

POSITIVE CONTROL on a purpose-built git fixture: a string tool_input '*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: .karta/binders/probe-k9.json
@@
-a
+b
*** End Patch' under tool_name Edit against a committed probe-k9.json exits 2 and names the binder on stderr
the same patch string against an untracked probe-k9.json exits 0 with empty stdout
the committed-binder denial also fires when the patch path is spelled with backslashes
the four Python gates stay clean: validate_plugin.py --self-test ends in PLUGIN INTEGRITY: PASS
oracle.command:
sh -c 'set -e; T=hooks/scripts/guard_binder_immutability.py; OUT=$(CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT="$PWD" python3 "$T" --self-test); python3 -c "import re,sys; m=re.search(r\"(\\d+)/(\\d+) checks passed\", sys.argv[1]); assert m and m.group(1)==m.group(2) and int(m.group(1))>=27, (\"self-test summary missing or under-floor\", sys.argv[1][-200:])" "$OUT"; python3 - <<\PY
import json, os, shutil, subprocess, tempfile
T = os.path.abspath("hooks/scripts/guard_binder_immutability.py")
g = tempfile.mkdtemp()
env = {**os.environ, "GIT_AUTHOR_NAME": "t", "GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL": "t@t", "GIT_COMMITTER_NAME": "t", "GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL": "t@t"}
def git(*a): subprocess.run(["git", "-C", g, *a], check=True, capture_output=True, env=env)
def run(ti, name="Edit"):
    return subprocess.run(["python3", T], input=json.dumps({"hook_event_name": "PreToolUse", "tool_name": name, "cwd": g, "tool_input": ti}), capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
git("init", "-q")
os.makedirs(os.path.join(g, ".karta", "binders"))
b = os.path.join(g, ".karta", "binders", "probe-k9.json")
open(b, "w").write("{}")
git("add", "-A"); git("commit", "-qm", "seed")
patch = "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: .karta/binders/probe-k9.json\n@@\n-{}\n+{\"x\":1}\n*** End Patch\n"
r = run(patch)
assert r.returncode == 2 and "probe-k9.json" in r.stderr, ("committed binder patch must be denied", r.returncode, r.stderr)
r = run(patch.replace(".karta/binders/", ".karta\\\\binders\\\\"), "Write")
assert r.returncode == 2, ("backslash patch path must still match", r.returncode, r.stderr)
r = run("just a string")
assert r.returncode == 0 and not r.stdout.strip(), ("non-patch string must pass", r.returncode)
git("rm", "-q", "--cached", ".karta/binders/probe-k9.json"); git("commit", "-qm", "untrack")
r = run(patch)
assert r.returncode == 0 and not r.stdout.strip(), ("untracked draft patch must pass", r.returncode, r.stderr)
shutil.rmtree(g, ignore_errors=True)
print("BINDER-GUARD-PATCH-OK")
PY
uv run scripts/validate_plugin.py --self-test'

work_items.title: guard_pack_write.py (Claude side) denies a patch-string write into a pack
work_items.summary: Port the Codex twin's patch handling into hooks/scripts/guard_pack_write.py so a string tool_input carrying an apply_patch body is parsed and judged like a dict write.
work_items.contract: EDIT hooks/scripts/guard_pack_write.py only. Keep it a single stdlib-only file. (1) NORMALIZE and (2) PARSE exactly as in binder-guard-patch-input: a str tool_input starting '*** Begin Patch' (after lstrip) becomes a patch command whatever tool_name is; parse_patch_ops with the same four directives, '\\'-to-'/' on paths, +/- content lines unable to spoof a directive. Copy the behavior from .codex-plugin/hooks/scripts/guard_pack_write.py. (3) JUDGE: for each op whose path resolves (against payload cwd) to a file this script already protects, apply the script's existing rule exactly as it applies to a dict write of that path; for an Add File or Update File op the content to inspect is the patch's + lines for that op, so any content-based check the script performs on dict writes runs over the same bytes. Ops on paths outside the protected set are ignored. Deny exits 2 with the existing message on stderr; allow exits 0 with no stdout. (4) FAIL-OPEN posture unchanged. (5) SELF-TEST: extend --self-test with at least: an '*** Add File:' string targeting a protected pack path is denied; an '*** Update File:' string on a committed pack is denied; the same Update string on a path the script does not protect is allowed; a protected path spelled with '\\' separators is denied; a non-patch string tool_input still passes. Summary line stays 'N/N checks passed' with N at least 19 (today 14). (6) No manifest change.

assertions: the script's own --self-test exits zero and its N/N summary parses with N at least 19
the script contains the '*** Begin Patch' sentinel and a '--self-test' entry point
a non-patch string tool_input against the repo root exits 0 with empty stdout
validate_plugin.py --self-test ends in PLUGIN INTEGRITY: PASS
oracle.command: sh -c 'set -e; T=hooks/scripts/guard_pack_write.py; grep -qF -- "*** Begin Patch" "$T"; grep -qF -- "--self-test" "$T"; OUT=$(CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT="$PWD" python3 "$T" --self-test); python3 -c "import re,sys; m=re.search(r\"(\\d+)/(\\d+) checks passed\", sys.argv[1]); assert m and m.group(1)==m.group(2) and int(m.group(1))>=19, (\"self-test summary missing or under-floor\", sys.argv[1][-200:])" "$OUT"; R=$(printf "%s" "{\"hook_event_name\":\"PreToolUse\",\"tool_name\":\"Write\",\"cwd\":\"$PWD\",\"tool_input\":\"just a string\"}" | CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT="$PWD" python3 "$T"); test -z "$R"; uv run scripts/validate_plugin.py --self-test'

work_items.summary: Correct the G3 record so it matches what shipped: Codex side verified live on zbook, Claude side verified by Windows Python self-test, live Claude-side run listed under G4 acceptance.
work_items.contract: EDIT docs/backlog/copilot-parity-gaps/FINDINGS.md only. (1) In the G3 section (heading 'G3: Patch-string input'), under 'Done when', state plainly that the Codex twins were verified live on zbook via PowerShell on 2026-10-03 and that the hooks/scripts/ twins are verified by running each script's --self-test under Windows Python on zbook; name the exact commands. (2) Add one acceptance check to the G4 section: with a consumer repo .claude/settings.json routing Edit|Write to hooks/scripts/guard_binder_immutability.py under Copilot on zbook, a patch-string edit of a committed binder is denied. (3) Do not touch the gap table row, the priority list, or any other gap's text. Keep the file's existing heading levels and table style (|-|-| separators, no padded hyphens). No agent attribution anywhere.

assertions: the G3 section names both hooks/scripts/ guard scripts and the phrase '--self-test'
no padded table separator (|---|) was introduced
no agent attribution strings appear in the file
oracle.command: sh -c 'set -e; F=docs/backlog/copilot-parity-gaps/FINDINGS.md; S=$(awk "/^### G3:/{p=1} /^### G16:/{p=0} p" "$F"); echo "$S" | grep -qF "hooks/scripts/guard_binder_immutability.py"; echo "$S" | grep -qF "hooks/scripts/guard_pack_write.py"; echo "$S" | grep -qF -- "--self-test"; awk "/^### G4:/{p=1;print;next} /^### /{p=0} p" "$F" | grep -qF "guard_binder_immutability.py"; ! grep -qE "\\|-{3,}\\|" "$F"; ! grep -qiE "co-authored-by|generated with|claude code" "$F"; echo FINDINGS-G3-OK'
